A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same monitoring framework and experiments. All 19 pages of each version, including figures, equations, Algorithm 1, and appendices, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of monitoring policies on generated BigCodeBench solutions and an additional test using backdoors from Wen et al. (2025).

after.justification: v3 retains these original policy evaluations, including the main experimental results and appendix distribution-shift results.

M1.justification: The exhaustive monitor-invocation search, Neyman-Pearson intervention allocation, stochastic single-monitor policies, and single-region two-monitor policy are unchanged. Algorithm 1 retains the same procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use 1,140 aligned BigCodeBench solutions, 318 generated backdoored solutions, and 300 sampled backdoors from Wen et al. The added discussion of biological and chemical misuse introduces no corresponding evaluation.

E2.justification: The same naive, likelihood-ratio, stochastic single-monitor, and always-both-monitor comparisons remain in the corresponding experiments, including the distribution-shift test. The NPS/NPR and BM/TM naming differences between prose and figure legends occur in both versions.

E3.justification: Section 4 retains the same Llama monitors, five-sample score averaging, preprocessing, KDE estimation, 218/100 misaligned train/test split, fixed aligned dataset, and experimental costs. The revised latency example in Section 3.1 is illustrative, not an experimental setting change.

E4.justification: The audit-cost sensitivity analysis, score-distribution illustrations, backdoor example, and distribution-shift test are retained. The latter moves from Appendix A.6.1 to A.7 without changing its analysis or Figures 8–10.

E5.justification: Both retain the 500-split default and 90% confidence intervals in Section 4.1, the 99-split annotations in several figures, and Appendix A.1's per-seed relative comparisons and bootstrap uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: All ten figures retain identical plot images, and the reported numerical findings are unchanged. For example, Section 5.2 still reports 71% monitor usage and a 2.4% overall audit false-positive rate at the stated $1.20 budget.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 corrects the worked cost-equivalence calculation: monitor latencies change from 10/1 ms to 1/100 ms, and the inconsistent c_a/c_1 = 10 statement is removed. The POMDP formulation, likelihood-ratio mathematics, budget equations, and appendix complexity derivation remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain budget-constrained recall optimization, two-stage policy search, more than doubling recall against a naive baseline, and Pareto improvements from combining monitors. The abstract's wording changes do not alter these claims.

C2.justification: The conclusion replaces explicit advice to develop complementary monitors rather than exclusively improve one monitor with a broader recommendation to combine monitors efficiently. The earlier complementarity discussion and limitations concerning distribution shift, overfitting, and scalability remain.

D1.justification: v3 adds explicit links to the authors' code repository and a practitioner guide for combining probe-based and black-box monitors. Prompts, implementation settings, hardware specifications, and runtime information are otherwise retained. The linked resources themselves were not inspected.

R1.justification: The introduction now explicitly positions optimization against heuristic multi-monitor systems, discussing OpenAI, Cunningham, McKenzie, and Parrack. v3 also adds Sharma, replaces Andrews with Lagziel and Lehrer for the screening explanation, and removes Parker and Pfister. The broader statistical and AI-control positioning remains.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites affect the abstract, introduction, related-work discussion, and conclusion. The distribution-shift subsection becomes Appendix A.7, with subsequent numbering and cross-references updated; the main narrative structure and most technical prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 6 now accompanies Appendix A.1 before A.2, and the backdoor-example heading appears on the same page as its code box. Other changes mainly concern spacing and page flow; all ten figures and Algorithm 1 retain their content.

improvement.justification: v3 corrects the inconsistent cost-equivalence example, clarifies the relationship to existing multi-monitor systems, and adds useful code and guide access information. These provide limited gains in accuracy, positioning, and reproducibility documentation. The scientific method and empirical evidence, including appendix robustness results, remain unchanged.
